featured_reviews.name: Grandpas Treasure
featured_reviews.review_text:
Wonderful nature getaway — worth the visit!

I recently visited Tungareshwar Wildlife Sanctuary in Vasai East and had a truly refreshing experience. The trails are lush and well-shaded, making the hike enjoyable even on warmer days. I loved how peaceful and green the sanctuary feels — it’s a great escape from the hustle and bustle of the city.

The views from the higher points are beautiful, especially during early morning or late afternoon when the light is soft and pleasant. I spotted quite a few birds, butterflies, and even some small wildlife, which was a nice surprise. The terrain has a good mix of easy and moderate paths, so whether you’re a casual walker or a bit more adventurous, there’s something for you.

Do come prepared with water, snacks and good walking shoes, because some sections can be steep and there aren’t many refreshment stalls inside. The local caretakers/forest staff were friendly and helpful when we had questions about the trails.

featured_reviews.name: Vikas Natekar
featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful and peaceful place for a quick getaway. Easy trek, lots of greenery, especially in monsoon.

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Naudiyal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tungareshwar Mahadev Temple is a peaceful and beautifully located temple inside the Tungareshwar Wildlife Sanctuary. The route leading up to the temple is surrounded by greenery, making the walk refreshing and enjoyable. It’s a lovely combination of nature and spirituality, and the overall atmosphere feels very calming.

You can reach the sanctuary by bike, car, or public transport, and from the entrance it’s a pleasant trek through the forest path. The temple is well-maintained, clean, and offers a very serene environment for prayer and relaxation.

Basic amenities like washrooms, drinking water, and small snack stalls are available along the way, which makes the visit comfortable. Parking is usually along the roadside near the entry point.

A wonderful place to visit for devotees, nature lovers, or anyone looking for a quiet break from the busy city life. Highly recommended.

I went in early monsoon thus there was less water in the river. Also there is a trek of nearly 7 km from the temple to top of Tungareshwar. You can sight many amphibians, reptiles and birds here.

featured_reviews.name: praniket more
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Mahakali Temple in Virar is truly a captivating spiritual destination. During my recent visit, I was mesmerized by the striking black stone Mahakali idol, which stands majestically as the focal point of the temple. Its imposing size and intricate craftsmanship imbue the entire space with a sense of divine energy and reverence. The idol’s presence is powerful, instantly drawing attention and inspiring awe in every visitor, whether a devotee or a curious traveler.
What truly sets this temple apart is its vibrant interior, where the walls are adorned with enlarged depictions of all Mahakali’s awtaras. Each avatar is rendered with remarkable detail and creativity, spanning the length of the temple walls in a mesmerizing visual display. These artistic representations not only tell the timeless story of Mahakali’s many forms but also contribute to a meditative and uplifting atmosphere. The interplay of traditional motifs and vivid colors create an immersive experience that leaves a lasting impression.
The overall ambiance is serene and welcoming, making it an ideal spot for reflection or prayer. Whether you seek spiritual solace, artistic inspiration, or a glimpse into Maharashtra’s rich cultural heritage, the Mahakali Temple at Virar is sure to be an unforgettable and enriching experience.

featured_reviews.name: Soniii
featured_reviews.review_text:
😊I visited Mahakali Mandir during Navratri, and it was an amazing and divine experience! 🙏✨ The idol of Maa Mahakali is very big — so tall and powerful that you instantly feel blessed after seeing her. This is a Sthanik Mandir, so you can visit anytime in the year, not only during Navratri.

But I will suggest going during Navratri, because the temple looks absolutely beautiful at that time. The decorations, lights, and the festive atmosphere make the place even more special. The Devi’s decoration during Navratri looks like a grand home — full of energy and positivity. 💫

If you ever get a chance, do visit once — especially during Navratri. You will definitely feel peace and positive vibes here. 🌸🙏

featured_reviews.name: SAHIL TIVAREKAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahakali Temple is truly one of the most peaceful and spiritually uplifting places I have visited. Nestled amidst a serene environment, the temple offers a beautiful blend of devotion, architecture, and positive energy. The moment you step inside, you can feel a strong sense of calm and divine presence. The idol of Goddess Mahakali is incredibly powerful and beautifully adorned, making the darshan a deeply fulfilling experience.

The temple premises are kept very clean and well-maintained. The staff and volunteers are courteous, helpful, and always ready to guide visitors, especially during peak hours or special occasions. The daily aarti is a major highlight—its rhythmic chants and devotional atmosphere create a mesmerizing experience that touches the heart.

Accessibility is also convenient, with clear signboards and parking facilities available nearby. On weekends and festival days, the crowd increases, so visiting early in the morning or late in the evening is ideal for a peaceful darshan. The surrounding area has small shops where you can buy flowers, prasad, and devotional items at reasonable prices.

What I appreciate most is the sense of community and devotion among the visitors. Whether you come here for prayer, meditation, or simply some quiet time, the temple offers an environment that refreshes both mind and spirit.

Overall, Mahakali Temple is a must-visit for anyone seeking spiritual comfort, cultural richness, or a moment of peace from daily life. Highly recommended for families, devotees, and tourists alike.
